---
title: "Validation against DWD phenology observations"
---

ThermoPheno 0.2.0 was evaluated against observed sowing and harvest dates for
maize, sugar beet and winter wheat in Germany. The run and data access date
were 22 November 2026. The protocol, inputs and station selection are the same
as for the 0.1.1 evaluation, whose outputs are
[archived](https://github.com/MR-Eini/ThermoPheno/tree/main/pkgdown/assets/validation/archive/v0.1.1) and compared with the new
results below.

## What changed in 0.2.0

In 0.1.1, `estimate_required_tt_from_observed()` summed triangular thermal time
over the observed planting–harvest interval without the winter-crop rules,
whereas the winter simulation applies its vernalization and dormancy rules.
For winter wheat the calibrated requirement was therefore larger than the
thermal time the simulation accumulates over the same observed season.

A diagnostic on the **calibration years only (1991–2010)** confirmed this. For
all 323 winter wheat station-seasons, the thermal time accumulated by the
simulation from the observed sowing date to the observed harvest date was
lower than the calibration sum (ratio median 0.844, range 0.685–0.930). With
the 0.1.1 requirement, the simulation could not accumulate the requirement
before the configured harvest deadline in 85% of calibration station-years.
For maize and sugar beet, which use summer rules, the ratio was 1 in every
season. The motivation for this check was the high number of forced winter
wheat harvests in the 0.1.1 held-out results. The diagnosis and the fix used
only the calibration years and synthetic tests. No code, configuration or
protocol decision was based on the 2011–2024 results.

In 0.2.0, calibration and simulation accumulate thermal time with one shared
internal function. The validation passes the crop's winter rules to the
calibration with `accumulation = "simulation"`, the new default. The old raw sum
remains available as `accumulation = "raw"`. Thresholds, planting windows and
harvest deadlines in the crop configuration are unchanged.

## Site selection and calibration

We used the DWD annual-reporter crop archives through 2024. The analysis
selected the DWD objects 215 (maize), 253 (sugar beet) and 202 (winter wheat),
and phases 10 (start of sowing) and 24 (harvest). Observations flagged doubtful
or incorrect were removed. Multiple reports within a crop, station, harvest
year and phase were reduced to the median date. For winter wheat, August to
December sowing observations were assigned to the following harvest year.

Within each crop, we ranked phenology stations with coordinates by the number
of valid planting–harvest calendars in **1991–2010**, breaking ties by station
ID. We attempted the first 25 stations with at least three such calendars.
Each was matched to the nearest DWD climate station with a historical daily
archive and station metadata spanning 1991–2024.

We calibrated one thermal-time requirement per crop and phenology station
using `estimate_required_tt_from_observed()`. The requirement is the median of
the seasonal thermal-time sums between observed planting and harvest in
1991–2010, accumulated with the simulation's rules (triangular thermal time;
for winter wheat also vernalization and dormancy). Calibration required at least
three seasons with temperature data for at least 95% of the observed interval
and a positive median. The
[crop configuration](https://github.com/MR-Eini/ThermoPheno/blob/main/validation/crop_config.csv)
records the temperature thresholds and scheduling rules.

## Held-out evaluation

We simulated planting from daily temperature and the crop's planting window.
Thermal time determined maturity. The configured harvest deadline could
trigger forced harvest below maturity. We compared dates with the paired
observations for **2011–2024**, requiring temperature data for at least 95% of
the configured season. A year without an eligible simulated date contributes
to the case counts and has no numeric error for that stage.

| Crop | Phase | Paired dates | Bias (days) | MAE (days) | RMSE (days) | R² |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Maize | Planting | 152 | 0.29 | 7.17 | 9.58 | 0.097 |
| Maize | Harvest | 152 | −7.34 | 15.32 | 19.58 | 0.252 |
| Sugar beet | Planting | 168 | −0.60 | 7.36 | 15.83 | 0.053 |
| Sugar beet | Harvest | 168 | −15.92 | 19.37 | 24.49 | 0.055 |
| Winter wheat | Planting | 217 | −8.76 | 10.39 | 13.49 | 0.002 |
| Winter wheat | Harvest | 217 | −1.79 | 9.45 | 11.12 | 0.269 |

Bias is simulated minus observed date. R² is the squared Pearson correlation
between observed and simulated days of year where both vary, a measure of
association. Harvest metrics include forced harvests. Station-years can share
climate stations, so the paired counts do not represent independent tests.

The sugar beet planting RMSE is sensitive to one anomalous DWD record. At
station 11908 in 2015, the reported sowing date (19 September) falls after the
reported emergence date (11 April). DWD flagged the sowing date as having no
objections. The main results retain this case under the stated quality filter.
Removing that record in a post hoc sensitivity check changes sugar beet
planting MAE from 7.36 to 6.34 days and RMSE from 15.83 to 7.90 days
(167 paired dates). Planting results did not change in 0.2.0.

## Comparison with 0.1.1

Both runs used the same 48 DWD input files (identical MD5 checksums), the same
75 attempted crop–station cases, the same station matches and the same
held-out station-years. Simulated planting dates are identical.

| Crop | Phase | Paired dates 0.1.1 → 0.2.0 | Bias (days) | MAE (days) | RMSE (days) | R² |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Maize | Planting | 152 → 152 | 0.29 → 0.29 | 7.17 → 7.17 | 9.58 → 9.58 | 0.097 → 0.097 |
| Maize | Harvest | 152 → 152 | −7.34 → −7.34 | 15.33 → 15.32 | 19.58 → 19.58 | 0.251 → 0.252 |
| Sugar beet | Planting | 168 → 168 | −0.60 → −0.60 | 7.36 → 7.36 | 15.83 → 15.83 | 0.053 → 0.053 |
| Sugar beet | Harvest | 168 → 168 | −15.92 → −15.92 | 19.37 → 19.37 | 24.49 → 24.49 | 0.055 → 0.055 |
| Winter wheat | Planting | 217 → 217 | −8.76 → −8.76 | 10.39 → 10.39 | 13.49 → 13.49 | 0.002 → 0.002 |
| Winter wheat | Harvest | 209 → 217 | 13.33 → −1.79 | 14.52 → 9.45 | 17.18 → 11.12 | 0.096 → 0.269 |

On the 209 winter wheat station-years with a simulated harvest in both runs,
harvest bias changed from 13.33 to −2.01 days, MAE from 14.52 to 9.36 days,
RMSE from 17.18 to 11.02 days and R² from 0.096 to 0.259.

| Winter wheat held-out outcome | 0.1.1 | 0.2.0 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Mature before the harvest deadline | 35 | 195 |
| Forced harvest below maturity | 174 | 22 |
| Failed to mature (no simulated harvest) | 8 | 0 |
| Insufficient evaluation weather | 2 | 2 |

Maize had 8 forced harvests in both runs and no failed seasons. Sugar beet had
no forced or failed harvests in either run.

One maize harvest moved by one day (station 10353, 2019: 6 to 7 September).
Its requirement differs from 0.1.1 only by floating-point rounding
(1099.275 versus 1099.2750000000003 °C·day). Daily thermal-time values from DWD
temperatures fall on a 0.05 °C·day grid, so a simulated total can equal the
requirement exactly. The order of summation then decides whether maturity is
reached on that day. 0.2.0 sums in the same order as the simulation.

## Attempted stations and exclusions

| Crop | Attempted station–crop cases | Insufficient calibration | No held-out calendar | At least one paired planting date |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Maize | 25 | 5 | 1 | 19 |
| Sugar beet | 25 | 1 | 3 | 21 |
| Winter wheat | 25 | 3 | 2 | 20 |

Eight sugar beet and two winter wheat held-out seasons lacked sufficient
weather. No winter wheat season failed to mature. There were eight forced maize
harvests and 22 forced winter wheat harvests.

## Interpretation and limitations

- Skill remains low. R² is at most 0.27 for any crop and phase, and below 0.10
  for every planting date and for sugar beet harvest. R² measures association,
  not agreement; bias, MAE and RMSE describe the size of the errors.
- Winter wheat harvest errors fell mainly because the calibration is now
  consistent with the simulation, which removed a systematic late bias. The
  simulated wheat sowing date remains about nine days early on average, with
  almost no association with observed sowing dates (R² 0.002).
- Sowing and harvest dates are partly management decisions. Farmers respond to
  soil workability, rainfall, machinery and labour, crop rotation and markets,
  none of which a temperature-only model represents.
- The early sugar beet harvest bias (about −16 days) was not tuned. Sugar beet
  harvest is largely scheduled by the processing campaigns of sugar factories,
  which the thermal-time maturity date does not represent.
- The winter wheat harvest deadline (15 August) still forces 22 held-out
  harvests. In the calibration years, 11% of the observed harvests at the
  selected stations fell after this date. The deadline was not changed.
- Winter dormancy and vernalization are simplified. Photoperiod, water stress,
  cultivar differences and frost kill are not represented.
- The sample favors stations with long calibration histories. Results describe
  this subset, crop configuration and climate-station matching procedure.
- Station-years share climate stations and calibrations, so they are not
  independent tests.

## Reproduce the run

Install ThermoPheno 0.2.0 and run the
[validation script](https://github.com/MR-Eini/ThermoPheno/blob/main/validation/dwd_validate_thermopheno.R)
from the repository root. Use the manifest to verify the DWD inputs. The
[calibration-period diagnostic](https://github.com/MR-Eini/ThermoPheno/blob/main/validation/diagnose_tt_consistency.R)
and the [run comparison](https://github.com/MR-Eini/ThermoPheno/blob/main/validation/compare_validation_runs.R)
can be run the same way.

```sh
Rscript validation/dwd_validate_thermopheno.R
Rscript validation/diagnose_tt_consistency.R
Rscript validation/compare_validation_runs.R
```
